claims.text: Vapor-depositing a thin Ni interlayer on W particles before spark plasma sintering with Cu will enhance wetting and bonding between the W and Cu phases.
The Ni interlayer will reduce void formation and phase separation in SPS-processed W–Cu.
The Ni interlayer will improve thermal transport and mechanical durability in W–Cu fusion-reactor heat-transfer joints.
Typical powder-metallurgy W–Cu materials exhibit phase separation, voids, and nonuniform interfacial contact.
The proposed Ni coating is tens to hundreds of nanometers thick.
The Ni-coated W particles are mixed with Cu powder and consolidated by SPS in an inert atmosphere.
The Ni interlayer acts as a wetting enhancer and diffusion mediator between W and Cu.
The Ni interlayer forms a graded W–Ni–Cu interface.
A graded Ni-containing interface minimizes interfacial-energy mismatch and void formation during rapid sintering.
Nickel has good wettability and solubility with both tungsten and copper.
Nickel promotes liquid-phase bonding of Cu around W particles during SPS.
Ni-mediated liquid-phase bonding enables near-complete densification and a defect-free W–Cu interface.
Improved W–Cu interfacial integrity will sustain high thermal transport and mechanical durability under irradiation.
Relative to SPS-processed W–Cu without an interlayer, Ni-coated W–Cu will have lower porosity and greater interfacial uniformity.
Relative to SPS-processed W–Cu without an interlayer, Ni-coated W–Cu will have higher thermal conductivity.
Relative to SPS-processed W–Cu without an interlayer, Ni-coated W–Cu will sustain greater mechanical strength under fusion-relevant irradiation.
Conventional SPS of mixed W and Cu powders without interfacial modification suffers from voids and phase separation.
SPS processing is restricted to temperatures below approximately 1000 °C to avoid Cu boiling and oxidation.
Long-term stability of the Ni interlayer under high-flux irradiation and elevated-temperature service remains unvalidated.
Prolonged high-temperature irradiation may cause unwanted intermetallic formation or excessive diffusion.

contradictions.description: The mechanism invokes liquid-phase bonding of copper during SPS, while the boundary restricts SPS to below approximately 1000 °C, below the normal melting point of Cu. No transient liquid, melting-point depression, or alternative liquid-forming phase is specified to reconcile these statements.
